description: Every constructor is counted, and constructors with no standings records get a count of 0. The average count per constructor is computed over all constructors.

b.request: For every constructor (including those with zero constructorStandings rows), count its constructorStandings records, compute the average of those counts across all constructors, and return the top 10 constructors by (count − average) with constructorId, nationality, record count, and difference, sorted descending by difference
b.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT c.constructorId, c.nationality, COUNT(cs.constructorStandingsId) AS record_count FROM constructors c LEFT JOIN constructorStandings cs ON cs.constructorId = c.constructorId GROUP BY c.constructorId, c.nationality), avg_count AS (SELECT AVG(record_count) AS avg_count FROM counts) SELECT k.constructorId, k.nationality, k.record_count, k.record_count - a.avg_count AS difference FROM counts k CROSS JOIN avg_count a ORDER BY difference DESC LIMIT 10;

a.request: Considering every constructor, with a count of 0 for those that have no constructor standings records, count each constructor's standings records. Compare each count with the average count over all constructors. Show the 10 constructors furthest above that average: the constructor id, its `nationality`, its record count, and the difference from the average (unrounded), largest difference first.
a.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT c.constructorId, c.nationality, COUNT(cs.constructorStandingsId) AS cnt FROM constructors c LEFT JOIN constructorStandings cs ON cs.constructorId = c.constructorId GROUP BY c.constructorId, c.nationality), avg_count AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM counts) SELECT counts.constructorId, counts.nationality, counts.cnt AS record_count, counts.cnt - avg_count.avg_cnt AS diff FROM counts CROSS JOIN avg_count ORDER BY diff DESC LIMIT 10

c.request: How many constructor standings records does each constructor have, and how does that compare with the average per constructor? Show the 10 constructors furthest above the average. Give the constructor id, its nationality, its number of standings records, and the difference from the average, largest first. Every constructor is counted, and constructors with no standings records get a count of 0. The average count per constructor is computed over all constructors.
c.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT c.constructorId, c.nationality, COUNT(cs.constructorStandingsId) AS cnt FROM constructors c LEFT JOIN constructorStandings cs ON cs.constructorId = c.constructorId GROUP BY c.constructorId, c.nationality), avg_c AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM counts) SELECT counts.constructorId, counts.nationality, counts.cnt AS standings_count, counts.cnt - avg_c.avg_cnt AS diff_from_avg FROM counts CROSS JOIN avg_c ORDER BY diff_from_avg DESC LIMIT 10;

d.request: For each constructor, how many constructor standings records does it have (counting constructors with no standings records as 0), and how far is that count above or below the average count per constructor, where the average is taken over all constructors? Show the 10 constructors furthest above the average, with each one's constructor id, nationality, standings record count, and difference from the average, sorted largest difference first.
d.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT c.constructorId, c.nationality, COUNT(cs.constructorStandingsId) AS cnt FROM constructors c LEFT JOIN constructorStandings cs ON cs.constructorId = c.constructorId GROUP BY c.constructorId, c.nationality), avg_c AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM counts) SELECT counts.constructorId, counts.nationality, counts.cnt AS standings_count, counts.cnt - avg_c.avg_cnt AS diff_from_avg FROM counts CROSS JOIN avg_c ORDER BY diff_from_avg DESC LIMIT 10;
